explainer.heading: A spot gel is stronger than an all-over cream — because it was never meant for the whole face
body: The concentrations in a spot treatment are calculated for a very small area over a short period. Spreading it across a whole region delivers several times the intended dose — and the usual result is dryness, flaking, and a weakened skin barrier.
A weakened barrier makes the next breakout easier. That is why some people find that the more they apply, the more persistent their acne becomes.
Dot the spot, leave it alone, and judge it in days rather than hours. If breakouts cover a whole cheek or the whole forehead, that is no longer a job for a spot gel — see a dermatologist.

items.heading: A few isolated inflamed spots
items.body: Exactly what this tube was made for: dotted onto each spot, not spread across the healthy skin around them.

items.heading: Breakouts across a whole area, or cystic acne
items.body: A spot gel cannot cover large areas, and cystic acne belongs with a dermatologist. We are not going to sell you that expectation.

items.heading: The spot has healed, only a mark remains
items.body: Post-acne marks are pigment, not acne. This is not the tube you need — see the mark gel further down.

blocks.heading: Seven ingredients, and why this is not an all-over product
blocks.intro: The formula concentrates its actives into a small area. That is why it works applied to the right spot, and why it does not suit whole-face use.

blocks.heading: Onto dry skin, before your moisturiser
blocks.intro: Order decides how much actually reaches the spot.

steps.label: Cleanse and pat dry
steps.note: Damp skin lets the gel spread onto the skin around the spot.

steps.label: Dot onto each spot
steps.note: A very small amount, covering the spot only. Let it dry.

steps.label: Moisturise everywhere else
steps.note: Avoid going over the dotted areas.

steps.label: Sunscreen
steps.note: Inflamed skin darkens very easily once it heals.

steps.label: Pat completely dry
steps.note: The step most often skipped, and the one that keeps the gel where you put it.

steps.label: Moisturise
steps.note: Keeping the barrier intact makes the next spot less likely.

blocks.footnote: No scrubbing, and no squeezing beforehand. Squeezing pushes the damage deeper and lengthens how long the mark lasts rather than shortening it. Patch test on the neck and watch for 30–45 minutes before the first use.

blocks.heading: Dab, do not spread
blocks.intro: The amounts below are taken verbatim from the manufacturer's instructions.

items.heading: A pea-sized amount for spots
items.body: Dab onto the spot or swollen area. For a larger area, two pea-sized amounts and no more.

items.heading: Let it absorb before the next step
items.body: Layering over gel that has not absorbed weakens both layers.

blocks.footnote: The manufacturer states plainly: using too much congests the skin, or dries and flakes thinner skin. This is a product where more does not buy more.

items.q: Can I use it all over?
items.a: Better not. The formula concentrates its actives for a small area; spreading it everywhere wastes product and readily dries thinner skin.

items.q: Can I use it alongside a pigmentation cream?
items.a: Yes, but not stacked in the same place. Dab the gel on the spot, let it absorb, then apply the cream elsewhere.

items.q: How long until I see a difference?
items.a: We do not quote a figure. Blemish-prone skin responds very differently from person to person, and one shared timescale would be wrong for most readers.

items.q: What about severe or cystic acne?
items.a: That needs a dermatologist, not a spot treatment.
